newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia president's popularity falling before poll.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia president's popularity falling before poll.

text.p: Mongolia's president, facing popular anger at the struggling nation's economic woes, has the support of barely one-quarter of voters with less than two weeks before presidential polls, local media said.
Support for President Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat, a candidate of the ruling reformist coalition, had slipped to just 27 percent on April 20, down from 34 percent one month earlier, a recent poll showed.

Challenger N. Bagabandi of the formerly communist Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP) had built a commanding lead before the May 18 election with 69 percent pledging support for him, the poll said.
That was up sharply from 53 percent in March, it showed.
Many voters were blaming Ochirbat for Mongolia's plague of economic worries such as rising unemployment and inflation, which soared again in March after cooling somewhat in previous months.
Bagabandi was also winning support with his charismatic and lively speeches that contrasted with Ochirbat's more measured speaking style.

Ochirbat's Democratic Union Coalition swept to a stunning victory in parliamentary polls last June, ousting the MPRP that had ruled the land of the steppes for 75 years, and moving to undo decades of Stalinst central planning.
